title: Run pane cues: queued runs, the orchestrator row, vendor/model/effort on every role row
lead:
*Proposed.* Drafted 2026-11-09 at HEAD 4707be4. Size: M recommended (the slice record says S; three cues, a wire field and golden views make it M, or split it, see Q4). Status: READY, with the owner's 2026-11-07 answers (all three cues). UI pass (rule u10) applies: `internal/tui`, goldens and `docs/dashboard.md` change.
Merged from S272 (vendor, model and effort on every role row).
findings_note: Owner 2026-11-03 (screenshot of the Running entry). (1) A run that is queued behind the cap shows the stale cue: s370 and S237 read '!! heard 32m' and '! heard 19m' although they have not started. lastHeard (internal/tui/relayboard.go:~167-190) ages the ledger run's updated_at, which nothing refreshes while the engine run is queued, so the row turns amber then red and looks hung. The docs only exempt a run that waits for a vendor slot (docs/dashboard.md:~535-538, S146/S169) and a wait on the owner (S154). Proposed: a queued engine run shows 'queued' or 'queued 19m' in the heard cell, dim, with no ! or !! cue. (2) The orchestrator step shows as the pane's live line ('- orchestrator start 32m', s443 on slicer) while the implementer, reviewer and gate rows are the work: the elapsed time is the relay's age, not a role's, and reads as a stuck orchestrator. Proposed: when ork runs the roles itself, show the orchestrator step dim with its state and no running clock; owner to confirm. Open owner questions: the heard text for a queued row, and whether the orchestrator row should hide or stay dim. A UI pass applies (u10); likely docs/dashboard.md and golden views change. Related: S146, S154, S169, S262. | Merged from S272 (vendor, model and effort on every role row): Owner 2026-11-03 (screenshot of the Running pane for s443): the orchestrator row shows no model or effort, and the queued reviewer and gate rows show only "queued". Fact: the orchestrator step is ork's own (agent ork, no vendor or model; docs/design.md:528), so it has none to show; the row should say so ("ork engine") instead of staying blank. The queued roles already have a planned vendor, model and effort in the run plan; show it on the row so the owner sees what will run before it starts. Open: whether a failed-over row also shows the row that was skipped. | Owner 2026-11-07: all three cues. (1) A queued row shows a dim 'queued 19m' with its planned vendor, model and effort, and no stale ! cue. (2) The orchestrator row is dimmed and labelled 'ork engine', not hidden, with no running clock. (3) A failed-over row shows the current entry plus a dim 'fell back from X'. A UI pass applies (u10).

sections.heading: Why
sections.body:
- Owner 2026-11-03 (screenshot of the Running entry): s370 and S237 read `!! heard 32m` and `! heard 19m` although they were queued behind the cap and had not started.
- Cause at HEAD: `engineLedger` copies the engine state into the ledger run (`internal/tui/relayboard.go:232`, `ledger.State = r.State`). `boardLive` returns true for `queued` (`relayboard.go:464-471`). `lastHeard` then ages `UpdatedAt` and adds `!`/`!!` past 10 and 30 minutes (`relayboard.go:166-190`). Nothing refreshes `UpdatedAt` while a run is queued. The docs exempt only a vendor-slot wait (`docs/dashboard.md:627`) and an owner wait (`:1912-1925`, S154).
- Owner 2026-11-07 (S267 findings): (1) a queued row shows a dim `queued 19m` with its planned vendor, model and effort and no stale cue; (2) the orchestrator row is dimmed and labelled `ork engine`, not hidden, with no running clock; (3) a failed-over row shows the current entry plus a dim `fell back from X`.
- Orchestrator row at HEAD: the pane tree prints the ledger step as `| orchestrator start  2m  codex sol high` (`internal/tui/runtree_test.go:58`, `:139`); the Running row takes the last `start` step's role and model (`internal/tui/overview.go:1015-1030`, `ledgerRunRow`), so an orchestrator step is shown as live work. `docs/design.md:528` says the orchestrator step is ork's own (no vendor or model); `docs/dashboard.md:1714` already words the matrix row `not run by ork`.
- Queued role rows at HEAD print only `. ROLE queued` (`relayboard.go:309`). The planned vendor, model and effort are on the record (`runrec.Record.Lineup`, `internal/runrec/record.go`) but `source.EngineRun` (`internal/source/source.go:263`) has no lineup field (`rg "Lineup" internal/source/source.go` finds none), so the TUI cannot show them yet: a wire change is needed.
- Fell-back row: `currentEntry` and `Roles` records give the current and the skipped rows (`internal/engine/engine.go:179`); `EngineRun.Roles` already carries each role's vendor, model, effort and exit (not re-verified field by field).
- adj: `adj check "ui.running-queued-cue"` returns `not found` (the slice key `running-queued-cue` is a slicer key); no decided record conflicts. Overlap: S146, S154, S169 and S262 are referenced (done or exempting); `slicer find "queued"` shows nothing open on this.

### Open questions

1. Queued age source. Options: (a) `CreatedAt` of the engine run (recommended: it is the moment it was queued, and is already on the wire); (b) a new queued-at field. Key: `ui.queued-age`.
2. Where does the planned lineup come from? Options: (a) a new `EngineRun.Lineup` copied from the record (recommended: the record is the single truth after a wave start); (b) the run plan call (`MethodRunPlan`) at render time (extra daemon call per frame). Key: `ui.queued-plan-source`.
3. A failed-over row with several earlier rows: (a) show only the last skipped entry (recommended, narrow width); (b) the whole chain. Key: `ui.fell-back-text`.
4. Split? Options: (a) one slice (as the owner answered all three cues together); (b) two: queued cue plus plan, then orchestrator plus fell-back (recommended if the golden diff is large). Key: `process.s267-split`.

sections.heading: Failing tests
sections.body:
In `internal/tui` (all in `queued_cues_test.go`).

- `TestQueuedRunHasNoStaleCue`: an engine run with state `queued`, `CreatedAt` 32 minutes ago, its ledger last updated 32 minutes ago. Assert `heardCell` is `queued 32m`, in the dim style, with no `!` and no `heard`. Fails first: it reads `!! heard 32m`.
- `TestQueuedRunAgeUsesCreatedAt`: `UpdatedAt` zero, `CreatedAt` 19 minutes ago: `queued 19m`; no `CreatedAt`: `queued`; a running run keeps `! heard 19m`.
- `TestQueuedRowShowsThePlannedLineup`: queued run with `Lineup` implementer claude sonnet high, reviewer codex sol medium: the pane tail rows read `. implementer queued  claude sonnet high`, `. reviewer    queued  codex sol medium` and `. gate        queued  codex sol medium`, dim; the pane's heard cell reads `queued 12m` (no `last heard`, no `ago`); a run with no plan keeps `queued` alone; the Running row line 2 reads `plan: implementer claude sonnet high`, dim.
- `TestQueuedRowsOfARunningRunShowThePlan`: a running implementer shows no plan row; its queued reviewer shows its plan.
- `TestOrchestratorRowIsLabelledAndHasNoClock`: ledger tree with an orchestrator `start` step (agent `ork`) 32 minutes old. Assert the node is `. ork engine` (no vendor, model, effort, phase word or `32m`), styled dim; the implementer, reviewer and gate rows keep their clocks; an orchestrator step with another agent keeps its text and is not labelled.
- `TestRunningRowDoesNotShowTheOrchestratorAsLiveWork`: when the only `start` step is ork's orchestrator, the Running row's role cell reads `ork engine` dim, with no model and no line 2; a later role step is live work as before; an orchestrator with another agent stays live work.
- `TestFailedOverRowShowsFellBackFrom`: implementer records codex `rate_limited` then claude: the row shows `claude sonnet` and a dim `fell back from codex sol high`; a role that did not fall back, the skipped row, a retry on the same entry and a role that finished ok show no suffix.
- `TestFellBackCueKeepsItsOwnLineInANarrowPane`: at 80 and 60 columns the cue does not fit beside the node, so the next line is the dim `    fell back from codex sol high`.
- `TestQueuedAndOrchestratorCuesInMono`: with `ASCII` and mono, the text carries the meaning without colour (`queued 12m`, `. ork engine`).
- `TestQueuedCuesGoldens`, `TestQueuedCuePaneGoldens`: new goldens for the Running entry and the three panes.
- Daemon: `TestEngineRunCarriesThePlannedLineup` (`internal/daemon/runs_test.go`): `EngineRun.Lineup` equals the record's lineup for a queued run.

sections.heading: Implement
sections.body:
1. Add the `Lineup` field to the wire row and fill it from the record. Keep it additive and `omitempty`.
2. In `lastHeard`/`heardCell`, handle `queued` before the quiet-time rule: dim `queued AGE` from `CreatedAt`.
3. Show the plan on queued role rows; label the orchestrator `ork engine` with no clock, dim; add the fell-back suffix from the role records.
4. Update `docs/dashboard.md`; rewrite goldens; review the diff.
5. Do not change the 10 and 30 minute rule for running runs, the owner-wait text (`waiting since`), the vendor-slot wait, `boardLive`'s other states, or any engine or ledger behaviour.

Owner decisions (2026-11-09, accepted the recommended answers): Queued age source -> (a) `CreatedAt` of the engine run (recommended: it is the moment it was queued, and is already on the wire) [ui.queued-age, adj 207]. Where does the planned lineup come from? -> (a) a new `EngineRun.Lineup` copied from the record (recommended: the record is the single truth after a wave start) [ui.queued-plan-source, adj 208]. A failed-over row with several earlier rows -> (a) show only the last skipped entry (recommended, narrow width) [ui.fell-back-text, adj 209]. Split? -> (a) one slice (as the owner answered all three cues together) [process.s267-split, adj 210].

Owner decisions (2026-11-09): Which orchestrator steps get the `ork engine` label? -> ork's own step only: apply the label, dim style and no clock only when the step has agent `ork` (`internal/engine/states.go:50`, `docs/design.md:683`). Other orchestrator steps keep their vendor, model and clock. `TestOrchestratorRowIsLabelledAndHasNoClock` and `TestRunningRowDoesNotShowTheOrchestratorAsLiveWork` set `Agent: "ork"` on the step, and a new test asserts that an orchestrator step with another agent keeps its text. [ui.orchestrator-label-scope].
